Governor Ivey Encourages Alabamians to Shop and Dine Local on Small Business Saturday

November 23, 2026

Press Releases

Share

MONTGOMERY –
 Governor Kay Ivey on Monday encouraged Alabamians to shop and dine locally on Saturday, November 28, as they make plans for Thanksgiving weekend and the Iron Bowl. Alabama’s more than 465,000 small businesses employ nearly half of the state’s private-sector workforce.

“I know that come Saturday, most Alabamians will be making their way to Bryant-Denny or settling into the lucky chair they have at home,” 
said Governor Ivey.
 “But the Iron Bowl doesn’t kick off until 6:30, so that gives us plenty of time to get out and support our small businesses. Stop by a shop downtown or pick up lunch from your favorite local restaurant. I am thankful for the folks who keep those doors open and give back to our communities all year long. This Saturday, let’s show them a little thanks of our own.”

Governor Ivey signed a proclamation
 earlier this month designating November 28 as Small Business Saturday in Alabama. The proclamation recognizes small businesses as “essential to Alabama’s economy, creating jobs, encouraging entrepreneurship and strengthening communities throughout our state.”

“I want to thank Governor Ivey for recognizing what Alabama’s small business owners do for their communities every day,” 
said NFIB State Director Rosemary Elebash.
 “She understands that when you support local shops and restaurants, you are supporting jobs in your community.”

According to U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) figures cited in the proclamation, Alabama is home to 465,610 small businesses. They account for 99.4 percent of all businesses in the state and employ 816,850 people, or 46 percent of Alabama’s private-sector workforce.

“Every purchase from a small business is an investment in the future of our community,” 
said Acting SBA Alabama District Director Jonel Hein.
 “This Small Business Saturday, we encourage Alabamians to shop and dine small, support local entrepreneurs and help keep more dollars working right here in our communities.”

Governor Ivey’s Small Business Saturday proclamation is attached.
